learning_outcomes.text: The student possesses essential concepts on the structure of simple microcontroller systems and on the architecture of a sensory node for IoT applications: from the detection of physical quantities via sensors to their input into the internet network. Knows the circuit specifications and fundamental programming techniques for using the most common peripherals integrated in modern 32-bit ARM microcontrollers (digital input/output, analog inputs, PWM peripherals, serial communication peripherals, etc.).
Knows peripheral interrogation techniques: (i) cyclic (polling); (ii) timed based on binary counters; (iii) event-driven; (iv) based on typical real-time operating system (RTOS) mechanisms.
The student possesses a basic knowledge of IoT protocols with which data can be exchanged between an electronic microcontroller system and the internet network.
The student possesses essential concepts on the realization of simple microcontroller systems useful for the circuit and firmware implementation of sensory nodes for the IoT network.
The student must be able to illustrate the theoretical and technical specifications that form the basis of microcontroller systems for IoT applications.

The student must demonstrate the ability to analyze simple firmware routines for interfacing with external sensors, process collected data, and appropriately send it to the internet network using one of the IoT protocols studied during the course.
The student must also be able to implement firmware to perform particular functions required in an IoT context.

The student must also be able to analyze some technical aspects of the electronic components used in the IoT, starting from datasheets and identifying the relevant specifications for correct hardware/firmware design.

syllabus_topics: Definition of IoT, IoT applications, IoT infrastructure, and the concept of an IoT node
Hints of Smart City, Smart Building, Smart Home, Smart Agriculture, Smart Mobility, Manufacturing 4.0
Microcontroller: definition, architecture, and difference from microprocessor
ARM architectures: history, CISC vs RISC
Digital Input and Output for STM32: GPIO Design, GPIO registers, and settings/functionalities
Analog inputs: definition, ADC, and STM32 micro case study
Operating modes, sampling frequency, polling techniques, interrupt, and DMA
Using ADC with the polling technique
PWM "pseudo-analog" signals: from digital to analog signal, filtering
Introduction to serial protocols: using the shift register
Introduction to I2C protocol: communication specifications, comparison with SPI protocol
Timing diagrams and differences with USART protocol
Introduction to the concept of interrupt as an evolution of polling
Concept of prioritized, masked, and nested interrupt
Protocols and standards for IoT: IoT network architectures, data protocols, and network protocols
Hints of OSI and TCP/IP models
Specifications and implementation of MQTT protocol
Overview of network protocols for IoT: short-range networks; medium-range networks; long-range networks
Comparison between different technologies: WiFi, Bluetooth, BLE, Cellular, LoRA
Electronic circuits for wireless connection to the internet
Introduction to Cloud services for IoT applications: Overview
Case studies based on cloud systems for IoT: realization of back-end configuration, user-app, actions, and data visualization
teaching_methods: Practical exercises for hardware implementation of embedded microcontroller systems and interfacing with sensors and the internet
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a computer-based test and an oral exam. The computer test assesses the ability to analyze and synthesize firmware for IoT applications or electronic schemes/components for IoT embedded systems. The oral exam assesses the understanding of theoretical methods for the analysis and synthesis of electronic microcontroller systems for IoT, both from a firmware and hardware perspective. The final grade is the arithmetic average of the scores obtained in the two tests. A minimum grade of 18/30 requires at least an elementary level of knowledge/competence in both the firmware analysis/writing part and the oral part. Students with excellent competence in both tests may be awarded cum laude.
bibliography: “Fast and Effective Embedded Systems Design: Applying the ARM mbed” by Rob Toulson, Tim Wilmshurst.
“Microcontrollers hardware and firmware for 8-bit and 32-bit devices” by Franco Zappa, Società Editrice Esculapio.
